svg.title: Consistent hashing on a ring
svg.desc: An animation in four steps. Database servers db-0, db-1, db-2, and db-3 each hash to three points on a ring, called virtual nodes, which cut it into 12 shorter arcs. Twenty players hash onto the same ring by player id, and each walks clockwise to the first point it meets. Egret walks to db-2#3, one of db-2's points, and the servers end up storing between 4 and 6 profiles each. A fifth server, db-4, hashes to three points that split arcs of db-3, db-2, and db-1, and takes 4 players: Heron and Otter from db-3, Petrel from db-2, and Newt from db-1. The other 16 players stay where they were, and the player counts show the loads ending between 3 and 5.
svg.text: Three points per server, its virtual nodes. The first point clockwise from a player stores the player's profile.
Three points per server, called virtual nodes. The 12 points cut the ring into 12 shorter arcs.
Egret walks clockwise to db-2#3, one of db-2's three points. Every player does the same, and the loads run from 4 to 6.
Server db-4's three points split arcs of db-3, db-2, and db-1. Each takes only the players between the previous point and itself.
The 4 moved players came from db-3, db-2, and db-1. The loads now run from 3 to 5, around the even share of 4.
